name: Bergisel-Schanze
kurzbeschreibung: The Bergiselschanze in Innsbruck blends Olympic ski jumping heritage with futuristic architecture by Zaha Hadid, an inclined lift, and a 360-degree panoramic tower.
preis: Adults €12.00, children (6–14) €6.50, groups €11.00; free with Innsbruck Card
oeffnungszeiten: Summer (June to October) daily 09:00–18:00; winter (November to May) Wed–Mon 09:00–17:00 (closed Tuesdays)
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Bergiselschanze stands prominently atop the storied Bergisel hill in the south of Tyrol's capital city, Innsbruck. The world-famous sports venue hosted the Olympic Winter Games in 1964 and 1976 and serves as the annual highlight of the prestigious Four Hills Tournament. The ski jump owes its unmistakable contemporary form to visionary architect Zaha Hadid, who sculpted a dramatic 47-metre-high tower rising like an organic sculpture into the Tyrolean sky. Visitors encounter an exhilarating blend of elite Olympic athletic history, masterly modern architecture, and a breathtaking 360-degree panorama: the sweeping view encompasses the dramatic Nordkette, the Zillertal Alps, the Wipptal, and the prominent Serles pyramid, right down across Innsbruck's historic old town.

Route & Requirements

From the stadium entrance, a modern inclined funicular carries guests up to the tower base in just two minutes. From there, a high-speed passenger lift takes visitors directly to the upper viewing terrace and the panoramic restaurant. Alternatively, energetic guests can climb the 455 open-air stairs to experience the vertical ascent on foot. The entire visitor centre and observation deck are designed with barrier-free accessibility, making it easy for families with pushchairs and wheelchair users. Comfortable, sturdy shoes are perfectly adequate for the outdoor tour. Encircling the stadium grounds is a well-maintained forest trail connecting the venue with the Tirol Panorama, the Kaiserjägermuseum, and the rugged Sillschlucht gorge.

Visit & Arrival

The Bergiselschanze is open year-round; during the summer months daily from 09:00 to 18:00, and during winter from Wednesday to Monday between 09:00 and 17:00 (closed Tuesdays). From Innsbruck city centre, visitors reach Bergisel via IVB tram lines 1 or 6 or the Sightseer bus to the Bergisel stop. Train travellers from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof can take regional buses or walk up in about 25 minutes. Drivers follow the Brenner motorway A13 to the Innsbruck-Süd exit; paid parking is available right below the arena.

Tips

Treat yourself to a visit at the panoramic "Bergisel Sky" restaurant, enjoying specialty coffee and homemade pastries with a dramatic view looking straight down the ski jumping inrun. During summer, guests can regularly watch professional ski jumpers practice on porcelain and plastic tracks. Entry is included free with the Innsbruck Card.
